text:
kevin: Quick heads up — while spinning up the new dedicated GPU nodepools in ap-southeast-2 we ran out of public IPs in the account. Pods fail on node bootstrap when we try to attach a floating IP. Need a quota bump request for public IP capacity and ENI attachments.

ashwin: How big is the gap? numbers pls.

kevin: Rough estimate — cluster autoscaler can add ~250 GPU nodes for peak tests. We currently have ~50 spare EIPs available. To be safe I want to request an additional 500 Elastic IPs and raise the regional ENI limit from 10k -> 20k. Also request increasing "vpc IP addresses per subnet" for the GPU subnets (we're hitting secondary IP exhaustion).

mariya: Can we avoid per-node EIPs? Suggest using NAT Gateway egress from a smaller pool of EIPs or use IPv6 dual-stack for outbound where possible. NAT GW has cost but reduces EIP churn.

kevin: Good point. For our workload we need some instances reachable from customer networks for testing (SSH/debug) so we still need a set of publicly-addressable nodes. But we can move the bulk of egress to NAT + IPv6. Request will include both EIP increases and enabling IPv6 on the VPC.

sam: FYI, AWS quotas we'll hit: "Elastic IPs (VPC)" and "Network interfaces per Region" and "IP addresses per subnet". They usually ask for business justification and sustained usage profile.

infra-bot: Created support case CASE-2026-04512 with AWS Support. Subject: "Increase Elastic IPs and ENI limits in ap-southeast-2 for GPU dedicated nodepools". Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home#/case?caseId=CASE-2026-04512

ashwin: thx. Can you paste the payload you submitted so I can reuse for other accounts?

infra-bot: Submitted body (trimmed):
```
We are Redwood Inference, launching Dedicated GPU nodepools in ap-southeast-2. Expected sustained peak: 250 GPU instances; typical ENI attachments per instance: 2 (primary + secondary IP for pods). Request: Elastic IPs increase to +500, ENI limit increase to 20000, increase of IP addresses per subnet from /24 -> /22 for two GPU subnets, and enable IPv6 dual-stack on the VPC. Business justification attached: production rollout, SLA-backed traffic, and on-call debugging needs. Contact: kevin@redwood.com, infra lead.
```

sre-oncall: AWS asked a follow-up: they want expected concurrency, AZ distribution, and whether we can use shared egress (NAT) vs per-node EIP. They also asked for a test plan for rolling back if limits cause networking impacts.

kevin: I'll upload a short doc: concurrency ~200 concurrent GPU nodes during peak, spread across 3 AZs (80/80/40). We will canary in one AZ first (Tuesday morning). Rollback plan: scale down nodepool to 0 and revert autoscaler.

mariya: Cost note — 500 spare EIPs will cost if left unattached. Estimate: $0.005/hour per EIP when assigned to a stopped instance or unattached (check current pricing). Consider requesting a smaller immediate bump (e.g., +150) and then ask for temporary increase for the launch week to validate.

ashwin: Agreed. Request both a permanent moderate increase and a temporary higher cap for the first 2 weeks. Include our monitoring hook so we can alert if EIP utilization > 80%.

kevin: Done — updated the support case with: permanent +150 EIPs, temporary raise to +500 for 14 days, ENI to 15k permanent with temporary to 20k, and IP-per-subnet increase to /22 for the two GPU subnets. Mentioned IPv6 opt-in.

infra-bot: AWS replied: ACKED, case in review. They requested the VPC IDs and subnet IDs and business contact. Please DM kevin the subnet list and I'll attach.

sam: I'll DM the subnet IDs. Everyone, please review the rollout plan in the doc I linked in the case. We should add a step to rotate node labels and mark nodes reserved so autoscaler doesn't spike unexpectedly.

kevin: Thanks all. If AWS approves the temp increase we'll proceed with the canary on Tue 09:00 APAC. Will post status here and follow up with cost estimate after the first 24h. :rocket:

mariya: :thumbsup: presuming case approval, I'll prepare a cost comparison NAT vs EIP-per-node and share before the rollout.

sre-oncall: Noted — oncall will monitor network metrics and BGP/route tables. Add pager rule if EIP allocation rate exceeds threshold.
